Design calls made without a prior Figma anchor, resolved this task: (1) active and expanded are mutually exclusive top-level looks (Figma: one `State` variant axis, 5 values default|hover|active|expanded|disabled) — an expanded parent never also renders as active, matching both references (neither showed the two combined); (2) active is colour-only, no background fill (icon+label recolour to `primary`), matching Stripe exactly; (3) hover reuses the existing-but-unconsumed Figma variable `background-hovered` (light `color/neutral/50`, dark `color/neutral/700`) — added to `packages/tokens/atlas.tokens.css`/`.json` and `atlas.figma.tokens.json` this task, the first code consumer; (4) child rows carry no icon and support exactly one nesting level (v1 does not support a second level of disclosure) — matches the Grok reference, which shows only one level; (5) badge/counter composes the existing `Badge` component (`size="sm"`) rather than a new Badge variant — Badge's existing variant/size/appearance set was sufficient; (6) no icon-only collapsed sidebar state — checked Stripe's own collapsed/narrow sidebar via Mobbin and found none exists (sidebar stays icon+label at all widths), so that state was dropped from the matrix entirely rather than guessed. A composed reference frame reproducing both Mobbin sources, plus explicit Light/Dark example frames and a Usage text block, live on the component's own `Sidebar Menu Row` page (not a separate page) — matching the established per-component page convention (see the `Spinner` page: variant grid + Examples — Light + Examples — Dark + Usage, all on one page). An initial draft wrongly put this on its own `Usage & Examples` page; corrected same-session per the user's catch, and that page was deleted.

decisions.topic: New content-width primitive scale (xs/sm/md/lg): app/page.tsx had no matching token for demo-block max-widths
decisions.decision: Sandbox audit (via atlas-verify's atlas-components hardcoded-length check, widened to app/page.tsx by this task) found 5 raw `maxWidth` pixel literals (240, 280, 400×2, 880) with no existing Atlas token to snap to — `--atlas-container-*` (640–1536px) is a page-breakpoint scale, an order of magnitude too large for a compact demo column or form. Per the user's explicit instruction (no hardcoded raw values), added a new primitive scale rather than reusing a wrong-fit token: `layout/content-width/xs|sm|md|lg` = 240|280|400|880, created in Figma `Atlas/Primitives` first (scope `WIDTH_HEIGHT`, matching `layout/container/*`'s own convention exactly), then mirrored to `packages/tokens/atlas.tokens.css` (`--atlas-content-width-{xs,sm,md,lg}`), `atlas.tokens.json` and `atlas.figma.tokens.json`. `scripts/atlas-sync.mjs`'s `LAYOUT_GROUPS` gained a `content-width-` entry so `atlas/tokens.md`/`tokens.json` list it. Values were chosen to exactly match the 4 distinct widths already in use (not rounded to a cleaner step) so no sandbox layout visibly shifted. Also snapped 23 hardcoded `letterSpacing: 0.06em/0.08em` occurrences in `app/page.tsx` to the existing `--atlas-letter-spacing-wide` (0.02em, a real value change to those labels' tracking — user chose this over adding new letter-spacing tokens) and 10 odd `fontSize` literals (13, 24, 0.75em, 0.875em) to the nearest existing `--atlas-font-size-*` step.

decisions.topic: Sidebar shell: collapsed state, mobile, and CSS approach
decisions.decision: B2 Sidebar shell uses a CSS data-attribute approach for the collapsed rail state: the Sidebar root sets `data-collapsed` on the `<aside>` element, and SidebarMenuRow's CSS module uses `:global([data-collapsed])` descendant selectors to hide `.label`, `.badge`, `.chevron` and center the icon — no React context needed for the visual collapse. Expanded width uses `--atlas-content-width-xs` (240px). Collapsed rail is 56px (3.5rem). Mobile/narrow viewport reuses the existing Drawer component (mobile web only, not native). References: Stripe dashboard (expanded layout, sections, footer), Grok (collapsed icon rail). Figma component set `620:52` with Collapsed boolean property and Light/Dark example frames.

decisions.topic: NavBar dashboard mode: breadcrumb + search slots, examples only in Figma (no Layout variant)
decisions.decision: NavBar (layouts) B3 Top App Bar upgrade adds two ReactNode slots — breadcrumb and search — for dashboard/app-bar usage, keeping the existing marketing layout (brand + links + actions) intact. No new Figma Layout variant property: the 48-variant explosion (Layout × Variant × Size × State) was rejected as too bloated; instead, example instances (Dashboard Light + Dashboard Dark sections) and an updated component set description with usage code show the dashboard pattern. Primary consumers are AI agents building prototypes, not human designers inspecting Figma variants, which justified examples over a variant axis. The slots render conditionally: breadcrumb after links, search with margin-inline-start auto. Dashboard mode is brand + breadcrumb + search + actions (no links, no hamburger). Both slots coexist with links if provided. No new tokens.

decisions.topic: Select: new primitives-tier component (CAND-003), scope and constraints
decisions.decision: Select (primitives) is a single-choice form control — role=combobox trigger + role=listbox popover — semantically distinct from DropdownMenu (role=menu, action trigger). v1 scope: sm (32px) and md (40px) sizes only (matching Input), single-choice only (no multi-select), no new tokens (reuses Input trigger tokens + DropdownMenu popover/item tokens). Built without a Radix dependency (DEC-016 precedent). Figma component set 630:75 with Size × State × Placeholder variant matrix (24 variants). Hidden .Select / Item sub-component (631:20, 6 variants). Compound API: Select, SelectTrigger, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectValue, SelectGroup, SelectLabel, SelectSeparator.

decisions.topic: Tooltip: new primitives-tier component (batch 3, B5), scope and constraints
decisions.decision: Tooltip (primitives) is a non-interactive hover/focus label. Reference: ReUI/shadcn Tooltip (node 42851:21668), mapped to Atlas tokens: fill foreground, text background (inverts in dark mode), padding spacing-3 / spacing-1_5, radius-md, arrow radius-sm (Atlas has no 2px radius), font-size-xs, z-tooltip. Figma component set 645:397 on the Tooltip page: Side = bottom | top | start | end plus a Text property. Side names the side of the trigger the tooltip appears on (Radix semantics; the arrow sits on the opposite edge), which differs from ReUI where Side names the arrow edge; start/end are logical and flip in RTL. ReUI's Kbd chip is out of v1 (needs a translucent-fill token Atlas lacks). Unlike Select (DEC-034, DEC-016), this uses @radix-ui/react-tooltip, approved by the user for hover/focus timing, collision flipping and aria-describedby. TooltipProvider defaults delayDuration to 300ms. No new tokens. Compound API: TooltipProvider, Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, TooltipContent.

decisions.topic: Label: Figma-first variant, optional marker and size drift fix
decisions.decision: Label (primitives) Figma set 50:48 gained Variant default | inline (identical drawing; inline only drops the block-end margin in code) and an Optional boolean with a (optional) hint text (12 Regular, foreground-muted; foreground-disabled when disabled), beside the existing Required boolean. Required wins over Optional in code. Drift fixed toward Figma (user, 2026-09-28): sm is 12px (font-size-xs), md 14, lg 16, and the label weight is SemiBold at every size (was Medium, sm was 14). decisions.topic: Bubble: new primitives-tier component, scope and token mapping
decisions.decision: Bubble (primitives) follows the shadcn Community Bubble reference (node 2360:4701, file bjcYqQP32iF9U6rwJ6gUqt). Figma page Bubble: set 656:27 = Variant primary | secondary | muted | tinted | outline | destructive x Align start | end (12 variants, Align draws identically; layout only) with a Text property; Bubble Reaction 656:28 with a Content text property; Examples Light/Dark and Usage frames. Collapsible 'Show more', Popover and the Tooltip example are out (compose Tooltip from the library). decisions.topic: Chart: new compositions-tier component on Recharts, scope and token mapping
decisions.decision: Chart (compositions) follows the shadcn Community Chart reference (node 296:42, file bjcYqQP32iF9U6rwJ6gUqt, Bar Chart - Interactive). Scope (user, 2026-09-28): the Chart card container (header with title, description and ChartStats toggle cells; content with loading and empty states; legend) plus a ChartBar plot built on Recharts, added as a dependency at the user's request (recharts ^3.10.1). The batch-3 plan (B7) listed a container only; the user widened it. Figma page Chart: Chart set 660:247 (State default | loading | empty; Title, Description, Stats and Legend properties), Chart Stat 660:9 (Selected false | true), Chart Tooltip 660:13, Chart Legend Item 660:10, Examples Light/Dark, Usage. decisions.topic: Toast: new compositions-tier component on Radix Toast, scope and token mapping
decisions.decision: Toast (compositions) follows the shadcn Community Toast reference (node 2011:2331, file bjcYqQP32iF9U6rwJ6gUqt), promoting CAND-004. Figma page Toast: set 670:68 = Variant default | success | danger (user, 2026-09-28: the reference draws one neutral style, the semantic variants are a design addition) with booleans Icon (off), Title (on), Description (on), Action (off), Close (on) and text properties Title text and Description text; Examples Light/Dark and Usage frames. decisions.topic: Table: new primitives-tier component family (Table head, Table cell, Table row), scope and token mapping

The reference's toolbar, sorting, row selection, column visibility and pagination are the composed example on the Figma page and the future DataTable (CAND-024, on @tanstack/react-table, no dependency added now). Figma page Table: Table head 674:68 = Content text | checkbox x Align start | end x Sort none | unsorted | ascending | descending (9 variants, none = not sortable), Table cell 674:9 = Content text | checkbox x Align start | end (3), Table row 674:137 = State default | hover | selected x Last false | true (6; Last is a variant because a boolean cannot drop a border), Data Table Examples Light/Dark, Usage. The sort control is an Atlas Button ghost sm and the selection control is an Atlas Checkbox sm. No aria-selected on rows (invalid on a plain table row). Code Connect maps all three sets; atlas-sync reads only the first (Table head).

decisions.topic: DatePicker: new compositions-tier component (single + range), scope and value-shape convention
decisions.decision: DatePicker (compositions) is inspired by the shadcn Community Date Picker reference (bjcYqQP32iF9U6rwJ6gUqt, node 73:226) as visual reference only — built directly into the Atlas file (cKYhfaHLCoyMHi9nKr63Ig), not copied from the reference file (user, 2026-09-29). v1 scope is single-date plus range selection; four further reference variants (dropdown month/year caption, Input-field variant, paired Time Picker, natural-language text entry) are logged as CAND-025..028, not built — each needs its own Figma design and, for natural-language, an explicit go-ahead to add chrono-node as a dependency. Figma page 'Date Picker': Date Picker 680:56 (trigger, State default|hover|focus|open|disabled|invalid x Placeholder true|false, 12 variants, mirrors Select's exact matrix), .Date Picker / Date 680:29 (day cell, State default|hover|selected|today|outside-month|disabled|range-start|range-middle|range-end, 9 variants), Date Picker Calendar 680:146 (single month: header + weekday row + date grid, reuses Atlas/Icons chevron-left/chevron-right), Date Picker Calendar (range) 688:391 (two months under one shared nav row), plus an Examples — Range Picker frame. Range value shape (user-approved, mirrors Slider's range pair, DEC-023): mode='range' makes value/defaultValue a [start, end] tuple rather than a {from,to} object, via a discriminated union on `mode` so single and range each get a correctly-typed value/onValueChange (this is why atlas-sync's props() extractor reports no own props on the DatePicker root — DISC-084 — the type is `type X = (A|B) & C`, not a plain interface). Range-middle fill geometry (user-chosen over a simpler independently-rounded-cell alternative): a seamless connected band — flat both sides by default (radius-none), re-rounded only at the true start/end and at each row-wrap edge (data-range-row-start/-row-end), verified in a Figma screenshot showing correct auto-reflow across row wraps. In range mode a grid's outside-month cells render blank (not the adjacent month's numbers) so the two months never show duplicate, ambiguously-clickable dates — a deliberate deviation from single mode, where outside-month cells stay real and clickable. No live hover-preview of an in-progress range (v1 scope): the picked start renders as a solid cell alone until the second click commits. No new tokens; two spacing values without an exact token (28px day cell/nav-button, ~18px weekday-row height) are composed via calc() from existing spacing tokens rather than invented. No popover dependency: the panel is portalled and anchored to the trigger, the same hand-built pattern as Select and DropdownMenu.

decisions.topic: DatePicker: dropdown month/year caption (promotes CAND-025)
decisions.decision: Adds captionLayout="label"|"dropdown" to DatePickerContent (single mode only — range mode ignores it and keeps the shared two-month text nav; a two-month dropdown caption was not requested and is not built). Figma: new component 'Date Picker Calendar (dropdown)' (691:592) — same anatomy as the single-month Date Picker Calendar (680:146), header swaps the plain text label for two Select sm instances (Month, Year) flanked by the same prev/next arrows; no changes to the Date Picker trigger or .Date Picker / Date states. New 'Examples — Date of Birth' frame (691:6049). Code: the dropdown caption is native <select> elements (not the compound Select component — a plain enumerable list needs no custom item rendering) styled to match Select's sm trigger via a wrapping .captionField + absolutely-positioned ChevronDown, not the native browser arrow. yearRange defaults to 100 years back / 10 forward from today (overridable), covering the birthdate use case without a hardcoded range.

decisions.topic: DatePicker: Input variant via new DatePickerInput subcomponent (promotes CAND-026)
decisions.decision: Adds DatePickerInput as a typed alternative to DatePickerTrigger — pairs Input (md) with a real, focusable trailing calendar button. Figma: no new component set; Input already has no Icon variant in Figma (icon slots are code-only, matching Input's existing convention), so this is documented as an 'Examples — Input' frame (692:654) composing an Input instance with a calendar icon overlapping its trailing edge, not a new formal Date Picker trigger variant. Code: the trailing button is a real sibling element positioned over the field's trailing inset, not passed through Input's trailingIcon prop — that slot wraps its content in aria-hidden (decorative-only by Input's existing contract, e.g. a loading spinner), which would hide an interactive control from assistive tech. Input does not forward a ref (repo convention, 'reach it by id'), so DatePickerInput finds the underlying <input> via a wrapper-div query on mount and uses that as both the panel's anchor and the focus-restore target. Typed text commits on blur or Enter via a caller-overridable parseDate (default: new Date(text), documented as locale-fragile); unparseable text sets aria-invalid and keeps what was typed rather than discarding it. Works in both modes via the existing mode-agnostic ctx.onSelect dispatcher; in range mode the field only ever shows/sets the range's start (documented — DatePickerTrigger + formatRange is the range-display path).

decisions.topic: DatePicker: Time Picker resolved as composition, not a component (resolves CAND-027)
decisions.decision: The shadcn reference's 'Time Picker' variant pairs its Date field with a plain text input ("10:30:00"), not a custom dropdown/scroll picker — re-reading the reference changed the original plan (a candidate TimePicker component) to: compose Input type="time" next to DatePicker (user, 2026-09-29). No new component, no new DatePicker prop or mode. Figma: no new component set — an Examples — Date + Time frame (694:927) on the Date Picker page shows the pairing, composed from the existing Date Picker trigger, Date Picker Calendar and Input (md) instances. Documented in atlas/DatePicker.md's DO and CODE sections.

decisions.topic: DatePicker: Natural Language Picker via new DatePickerNaturalInput, adds chrono-node (promotes CAND-028)
decisions.decision: Adds DatePickerNaturalInput, a free-text alternative to DatePickerTrigger parsed via chrono-node ('in 2 days', 'next Friday'). chrono-node added as a new dependency with explicit user approval (AGENTS.md §4/§7, user 2026-09-29) — introduces 0 new vulnerabilities per npm audit (checked before use). Figma: no new component set — Input has no Icon/plain-text trigger variant to draw (same reasoning as DatePickerInput, DEC-043); documented as an 'Examples — Natural Language' frame (695:831): a bare Input, a preview line below it, and the existing single-month Calendar. Code: chrono re-parses on every keystroke for a live preview line only (renderPreview, default 'Selected: {date}'); the field itself commits on blur/Enter like DatePickerInput and keeps the typed phrase rather than reformatting it into a calendar-style string — reformatting would defeat the point of typing a phrase. Opens the panel on focus (onFocus, unlike every other trigger type) as a persistent visual reference while typing, matching the reference. Bug found and fixed during testing: committing via Enter calls onSelect, which refocuses the trigger element (existing shared behaviour for every trigger type) — but since this trigger's own onFocus reopens the panel, that refocus stole focus to the dialog, blurring the field and firing a second, spurious commit. Fixed with a justCommittedRef guard consumed by the next focus event, not by changing the shared onSelect/refocus behaviour other trigger types rely on. Same mode-agnostic ctx.onSelect dispatcher as the other triggers; in range mode only sets the range's start, same documented limitation as DatePickerInput.

decisions.topic: DatePicker: fix focus-trap bug in DatePickerInput/DatePickerNaturalInput blur-commit
decisions.decision: Bug (found after the DatePickerNaturalInput focus-loop fix in DEC-045, while checking for related issues): ctx.onSelect unconditionally called triggerRef.current.focus() after every commit, restoring focus to the trigger — correct when the commit came from clicking a calendar cell (a different element had focus), but wrong when DatePickerInput or DatePickerNaturalInput's OWN blur handler calls commit — calling .focus() on an element from inside its own blur handler fights the browser's pending focus change (Tab-away, click-away) and snaps focus back into the field, a documented real-browser anti-pattern not visible via jsdom's activeElement (fireEvent.blur does not itself move document.activeElement in jsdom, confirmed empirically — the regression test spies on .focus() instead). Fix: ctx.onSelect / onSelectSingle / onSelectRangeDay take an optional restoreFocus (default true) parameter; DatePickerInput and DatePickerNaturalInput pass false from their blur handler and true from their Enter handler (matching prior behaviour there — the field is already focused, so it's a no-op either way). The grid's two call sites (cell click, Enter-in-grid) are unchanged (default true). Two regression tests added (one per component) spying on the field's .focus() method.

decisions.topic: DatePicker: three bugs found by /code-review on PR #1, all confirmed and fixed
decisions.decision: Ran /code-review on PR #1 (the DatePicker PR) at the user's request; each of its three findings was independently reproduced with a throwaway test before fixing (one, on activeElement, was itself unreliable in jsdom and rewritten as a focus() spy — see the test files for the reproduction methodology, not kept in the repo). (1) DatePickerNaturalInput's onFocus reopened the panel after ANY programmatic restore-focus, not just its own commit — the local justCommittedRef guard (DEC-045) only covered its own commit() path, so selecting a date from the grid or pressing Escape closed the panel and then immediately reopened it, since onSelectSingle/onSelectRangeDay/closeAndRestoreFocus all call triggerRef.current.focus() too. Fixed by moving the guard onto the shared context as suppressNextFocusOpen, set by every restore-focus call site (both onSelect functions, and DatePickerContent's closeAndRestoreFocus), consumed by DatePickerNaturalInput's onFocus; the local justCommittedRef is removed. (2) focusDate() only ever shifted the visible month by one when the newly-focused date fell outside the rendered grid, so Shift+PageUp/PageDown (a full year, i.e. up to 12 months) left focusedDate on a date that isn't rendered anywhere — pendingFocusRef's DOM lookup silently finds nothing. Fixed by jumping directly to the month that makes the target date visible, computed from the date itself rather than stepped by one. (3) DatePickerInput's resync-from-committed-value effect was gated only on `dirty`, which is deliberately never cleared after a failed parse (so the invalid text stays visible, per its own contract) — but that meant the effect stayed permanently disabled even after a later, genuinely NEW value was committed elsewhere (e.g. picking a date from the grid), leaving the field stuck showing stale invalid text. Fixed by additionally tracking the last-synced anchor's timestamp and forcing a resync whenever the anchor's actual value changes, regardless of dirty. Three new regression tests added (one per bug), all verified failing before the fix and passing after.

decisions.topic: AlertDialog built as a new component, distinct from Dialog
decisions.decision: User request (ref: shadcn-ui-components-vanilla-library Figma, node 72-2675) to add AlertDialog. Atlas's existing Dialog already covers confirm/destructive use cases via a `destructive` variant, so the agent asked whether to refine Dialog or add a genuinely new component; user chose new component and explicitly clarified "dialog is not equal to alert dialog" — rejecting a thin AlertDialog-wraps-Dialog composition. Built as its own Figma component set (node 700:6560, page "AlertDialog") cloned from Dialog's 12 variants with the header close-X stripped, and its own code on `@radix-ui/react-alert-dialog` (role="alertdialog", distinct from Dialog's role="dialog"; blocks outside-click dismissal but Escape still closes it, matching Radix's actual default — not "no dismiss by Escape" as first drafted). New peer dependency `@radix-ui/react-alert-dialog` added to packages/ui-web/package.json.

decisions.topic: Tabs: outline variant, vertical orientation as example (not a variant axis), and Icon/Badge properties added
decisions.decision: User request (ref: shadcn-ui-components-vanilla-library Figma, node 73:2899) to add variants to Tabs. Scope confirmed with the user (2026-09-29): (1) a new `outline` TabsVariant, matching the reference's 'Default' style — identical to `segmented`'s per-trigger states except no track background (hover has no fill, vs segmented's background-muted); 15 new variants added to component set 146:54 (line|pill|segmented|outline × sm|md|lg × 5 states = 60 total), cloned from `segmented` with only the hover fill stripped. No new tokens. (2) `orientation` (`horizontal`|`vertical`) added as a code-only prop on TabsRoot/TabsList, NOT a crossed Figma variant — exploding all 60 trigger variants ×2 was rejected as bloat for a layout-only change with zero per-trigger visual delta, following the NavBar/DEC-033 precedent of an Examples frame over a variant axis; an 'Examples — Vertical' frame was added to the Tabs page instead, composed from existing `pill` instances. Radix's native `orientation` prop handles the Up/Down roving-focus swap and aria-orientation automatically; the line variant's sliding indicator gained a vertical (inline-start rail) CSS path. (3) Separately investigated and closed in the same task (DISC-088): the shadcn reference's Tab component has real Icon/Badge boolean properties that Atlas's Figma trigger never drew, even though `TabsTrigger.leadingIcon`/`badge` already shipped in code — user chose to add it to this task rather than defer. Added directly to component set 146:54 (not per-variant-component, since ComponentSetNode also implements ComponentPropertiesMixin): `Icon` (boolean, default off) + `Icon slot` (instance-swap, default Atlas/Icons `circle-check`), and `Badge` (boolean, default off, wired to an appended Atlas `Badge` `neutral`/`sm`/`default` instance) — mirrors Button's DEC-024 Leading icon/slot pattern. No code change needed for Icon/Badge; Code Connect updated to map both.

decisions.topic: CodeBlock scope: static + typing variants, no syntax highlighting, web only
decisions.decision: User request (ref: animate-ui.com Code Block primitive) to add a CodeBlock. Scope confirmed with the user (2026-09-30): (1) two variants, `default` (full code) and `typing` (typewriter with a blinking cursor, drawn mid-write in Figma), crossed with sm|md|lg (6 variants; node 731:108, page "Code Block"); (2) no syntax highlighter and no new dependency — plain monospace text on existing semantic tokens, Light and Dark free; (3) parts: copy button (existing Button + AnimatedIcon check), header with filename/language, optional line numbers with auto-width gutter; (4) typing duration defaults to 5000ms like the reference; (5) web only, native parity in candidates.json (CAND-028). Built in compositions/CodeBlock. No new tokens.

decisions.topic: ScrollProgress: a new primitive distinct from Progress; page and container scope; web only
decisions.decision: User request (ref: animate-ui.com Scroll Progress primitive). Scope confirmed with the user (2026-09-30): (1) a new ScrollProgress primitive, not a Progress variant — Progress stays task completion (role=progressbar, always exposed), ScrollProgress is bound to scroll position and decorative by default; (2) Figma set 734:27 (page "Scroll Progress"): Orientation horizontal|vertical x Scope page|container x Progress 0|50|100 (12 variants); Progress is a drawn level only because Figma cannot show a live scroll value, so it is not a code prop; (3) Scope=page is a flat fixed strip on the viewport edge, Scope=container is placed by the caller and tracks a `target` ref (user chose page, container and vertical orientation); (4) `axis` (scroll direction measured, default vertical) is a code-only, non-visual prop so a horizontal bar can track a vertical scroll; (5) motion tracks scroll directly and eases with duration/fast and easing/standard, no spring and no new token (user chose token-based ease over the reference's spring); reduced motion sets the fill with no transition; (6) thickness fixed at spacing/1 (4px), no size axis; (7) web only, native parity in candidates.json (CAND-029). No new tokens.
